Requirement: Execute one bounded chunk with recorded scope, acceptance, verification and state before the next chunk.
Commit all meaningful sources, models, testbenches and essential reproducibility evidence to Git.
Identify and record unvalidated numerical targets and assumptions rather than inventing PDK/IP values.
Complete and commit a recent source-grounded literature survey before choosing any block architecture or implementation.
Target_or_Limit: Before design of each new/materially changed block

Requirement: Extract normalized measured literature benchmarks separately from simulations and vendor typical values.
Link each literature finding to an implication and design decision with relevant requirement IDs.
Document a quantitative before/after area and power comparison and prove hard constraints remain satisfied for substantial optimizations.
Record nontrivial architecture choices with alternatives, evidence, risk and revisit trigger in an ADR.
Maintain stable requirement IDs and bidirectional paths to design and verification evidence.
Do not claim that an unverified target or generated layout is tapeout-ready.
Do not bypass a failed review gate without a documented, approved waiver.
Re-survey a block when architecture/process/requirements materially change or the pre-tapeout review is older than twelve months.
Reproduce results with inputs, scripts, tool versions, corners, random seeds and checksums as relevant.
Exclude licensed PDK/IP, foundry decks, secrets, personal physiological data and unlicensed paper PDFs from the public repository.
Maintain current branch, chunk, blocked work, validation result and exact next action in project state.
Create and maintain golden models for energy, biosignal/optical/thermal/electrochemical noise, data rate, memory and timestamps before implementing applicable blocks.
Run public CI checks for model regressions, requirements integrity, RTL lint and simulation as tool access allows.
Record risk owner, impact, mitigation and next evidence for high-risk system items.
For each major review record agenda, inputs, findings, actions, gate result and closure evidence.
Keep selected assumptions and foundry/IP values marked TBD until confirmed by vendor/PDK evidence.
Classify each numeric assertion as target, limit, placeholder or TBD until verified with units and operating conditions.
Cover analog corners, startup, overload, shutdown, mismatch and post-layout effects as applicable before design signoff.
Cover digital lint, simulation, reset/CDC and appropriate assertions/coverage before design signoff.
Complete SRR, SAR, PDR, CDR, prelayout, postlayout and tapeout reviews with findings and closure logs at their relevant gates.
Do not proceed to tapeout without independent foundry/IP and DRC/LVS/ERC/PEX/STA/EM-IR/reliability closure.
Bound all operating modes by body-connected safety and valid measurement rather than reducing those constraints to save area or power.
Select a die/package partition by quantitative evaluation of noise, energy, yield, RF, MEMS, NRE and process fit.
Evaluate a heterogeneous SiP as one externally usable physiological module.
Keep nRF-class MCU/radio external to custom Gen-1 silicon unless a reviewed trade study supports integration.
Retain a specialized MEMS IMU rather than fabricating its mechanics on the custom analog die.
Support synchronized biopotential, electrodermal, electrochemical, optical, inertial, acoustic and thermal research interfaces where feasible.
Distinguish electrical capability from validated biomarker accuracy in all sensor claims.
Provide research/raw data access and calibration metadata for proposed multimodal inference.
Enable sleep, cardiovascular, daily health, biochemical, optical, audio and raw research modes according to product priority.
Quantify and verify every supported simultaneous sensor combination against power, peak current, ADC, pin and data constraints.
Preserve a ten-percent usable custom-die core area reserve at architecture freeze.
Prevent unreviewed consumption of the approved future area reserve.
Reserve spare package routing, power/ground contacts, signals and thermal headroom when feasible.
Reserve configurable analog inputs, electrode-capable inputs and excitation DAC outputs when feasible.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET 2–4 analog inputs; 2 electrode inputs; 2 DAC outputs

Requirement: Retain synthesized digital area reserve at subsystem signoff.
Retain worst-concurrency average memory bandwidth reserve.
Reserve interrupt IDs, register addresses and DMA extensibility.
Minimize energy per sample, event and moved bit within validated signal and safety bounds.
Minimize die/package footprint, height and external component count subject to yield, thermal and RF constraints.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET package 6–8 mm × 6–8 mm; height ≤1.2 mm aspirational

Requirement: Treat medical/clinical claims such as cuffless BP as research only until validated against suitable reference methods.
Target_or_Limit: No clinical claim by hardware alone

Requirement: Provide truly simultaneous differential EEG/ECG acquisition with independently specified signal path quality.
Allow each selected channel to configure an EEG or ECG profile and electrode routing.
Maintain high effective electrode input impedance over the measurement band.
Limit input bias and pad/mux leakage under dry-electrode source impedance.
Accept differential physiological inputs with specified artifacts and electrode common mode.
Tolerate electrode DC offset without losing specified signal quality.
Reject common-mode interference under a specified source-imbalance and frequency test.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET CMRR >100 dB; test conditions TBD

Requirement: Meet integrated input-referred EEG noise over a stated band and with a stated source impedance.
Support configurable end-to-end gain without excessive noise or saturation.
Provide EEG passband and configurable high/low-pass behavior with anti-aliasing.
Provide ECG passband and configurable high/low-pass behavior with anti-aliasing.
Explore extended biopotential research bandwidth if power and noise permit.
Provide configurable per-channel output sampling options.
Provide higher-rate biopotential research sampling if power permits.
Specify converter performance by input noise, SNR, SNDR, ENOB and bandwidth instead of nominal word length.
Detect saturation and recover within a specified interval.
Detect electrode open/contact impedance and report measurement state.
Evaluate low-leakage electrode switching with ESD, capacitance and charge-injection error.
Specify biopotential PSRR under analog rail and DC/DC spur conditions.
Specify differential input dynamic range, overload recovery and sample quality flag behavior.
Limit body electrode currents in hardware in every reset and firmware state.
Target_or_Limit: Safe current limit TBD by qualified review

Requirement: Provide independently configurable electrodermal/bioimpedance channels.
Measure DC conductance/EDA and electrode/contact impedance.
Support programmable AC bioimpedance excitation and synchronous receive.
Evaluate excitation frequency coverage against tissue/electrode models and power.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET 0.1 Hz–1 MHz; upper bound provisional

Requirement: Support a programmable impedance voltage/TIA receive path with saturation reporting.
Provide synchronous I/Q or equivalent magnitude/phase estimation where justified.
Support capacitive on-body/contact sensing with controlled excitation and quality metadata.
Provide a calibration loopback to separate front-end error from sensor impedance.
Provide configurable electrochemical channels for potentiometric and amperometric use.
Provide full three-electrode potentiostat paths when supported by selected chemistry.
Support high-impedance potentiometric measurement independently of drive mode.
Provide ISE voltage-buffer impedance at low frequency with defined test conditions.
Limit potentiometric input bias below electrode error budget.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET pA-class or lower if feasible

Requirement: Allow differential potential relative to reference electrode and its allowed common mode.
Support Na/K/pH/Cl ISE slope, offset and temperature calibration in digital processing.
Retain raw electrode mV and calibration identity for independent concentration modeling.
Measure signed electrochemical current over calibrated ranges.
Provide programmable TIA ranges, auto-ranging, overload indication and recovery.
Control working/reference/counter electrode potentials with a precision bias DAC.
Support open-circuit potential measurement without cell polarization from the circuit.
Support bounded waveform primitives for chronoamperometry and voltammetric research.
Support electrochemical impedance spectroscopy if the electrode and energy budget justify it.
Characterize shared reference and multiplexing leakage/polarization and cross-talk.
Support per-electrode two-point and multi-point calibration records without hard-coded analog concentration conversion.
Quantify Nernst slope variation, interfering ions and temperature dependence for the chosen ISE chemistry.
Apply independent hardware limits to cell excitation/current under faults or reset.
Target_or_Limit: Bounds TBD by chemistry and safety review

Requirement: Provide temperature and reference-drift metadata for Na/K calibration.
Expose sweat conductivity/rate auxiliary inputs subject to actual transducer availability.
Avoid claims of glucose/hormone accuracy without chemistry and human reference validation.
Support independent programmable optical source outputs if concurrency/pins allow.
Program calibrated per-source peak current within a hardware envelope.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET 0–150 mA peak; source/package thermal limit TBD

Requirement: Control LED current with stated effective resolution and temperature dependence.
Control source sequencing, phase and pulse width with synchronized receive timing.
Detect LED open/short and disable a faulted high-current path.
Provide independent source enables and time-multiplexed wavelengths.
Accept multiple PD current inputs with independently defined capacitance and dark current.
Acquire concurrently when optical spatial timing demands it.
Provide selectable effective optical input gain or integration span.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET equivalent TIA ≈1 kΩ to >10 MΩ

Requirement: Reject or measure ambient and dark optical signal without corrupting the desired pulsatile signal.
Report optical saturation and restore valid acquisition after overload.
Characterize photodiode capacitance, dark current, shot noise and TIA input noise at each intended wavelength.
Measure and subtract baseline ambient and dark samples with documented motion and light-change residual.
Time-associate wavelength, source current, PD ID, gain and integration time with samples.
Support multiwavelength reflectance and red/NIR PPG research with raw calibrated samples.
Support weak fluorescence/autofluorescence readout with dark subtraction and optical filtering.
Keep UV output disabled until independent hardware exposure limits and optical calibration are established.
Enforce a calibrated, cumulative UV exposure bound independently of host firmware when UV is implemented.
Verification_Method: Fault injection and optical power test

Requirement: Enforce source overcurrent and thermal interlocks independently of firmware.
Optimize source current, gain, integration and duty cycle for SNR per energy within saturation bounds.
Treat Raman spectroscopy as a separate feasibility effort rather than assuming LED and PD alone suffice.
Do not equate multispectral sensor readings alone with validated hemoglobin, melanin or AGE biomarkers.
Provide slow precision thermal/auxiliary inputs subject to package and ADC availability.
Support duty-cycled, ratiometric NTC excitation with self-heating quantified.
Store NTC calibration coefficients for temperature calculation.
Provide a DC-capable thermopile/heat-flux interface for a kΩ source and ≈100 µV representative output.
Limit thermal-path input offset over specified source impedance and temperature.
Limit thermal-path input offset drift over specified temperature and aging.
Limit integrated low-frequency thermal input noise under a specified measurement procedure.
Provide programmable thermopile gain without loss of DC information.
Provide selectable heat-flux measurement bandwidth.
Quantify chopping ripple, drift and settling effects on thermal measurements.
Provide a configurable combination of analog/PDM/contact audio inputs subject to pin and power limits.
Support analog mic bias, programmable gain and antialiasing with characterized noise.
Support digital PDM clocking and decimation where selected microphones require it.
Support a high-impedance or charge-amplifier contact/piezo input when selected.
Provide audio ADC sampling for proposed recording modes.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET 48 kHz; 96 kHz optional; 24-bit class label

Requirement: Deliver a full-range electrical audio path if selected; actual actuator bandwidth is separately specified.
Evaluate Class-D electromagnetic versus high-voltage piezo actuation against transducer, safety and power limits.
Implement click/pop control, mute, gain and overdrive limiting for selected audio output.
Evaluate 48/96 kHz audio DAC and processing precision by noise/distortion rather than word length alone.
Supply audio filtering and limiting primitives only if selected product modes justify energy and area.
Bound audio duty cycle and peak power by usable battery energy and thermal limits.
Evaluate 8 truly simultaneous low-frequency biopotential converters against channel noise, area and power needs.
Evaluate dedicated versus shared electrochemical precision conversion under leakage and concurrency requirements.
Provide optical conversion capacity for approved spatially simultaneous modes.
Provide thermal/precision conversion resources matched to chosen sensors.
Provide fast research ADCs only if concrete uses justify area/energy.
Specify each selected ADC by full scale, common mode, bandwidth and sample rate.
Verify each ADC noise, SNR, SNDR, THD, INL, DNL and ENOB at stated input and clock conditions.
Verify each ADC power, area, startup, calibration, reference/clock sensitivity and PVT yield.
Provide precision programmable voltage biases for selected excitation/calibration needs.
Program independently selected optical source currents within calibrated bounds.
Provide high-rate waveform channels only when impedance/stimulation uses justify their cost.
Verify monotonicity, INL/DNL, noise, settling, glitch, drive, range and drift under specified conditions.
Map simultaneous sensor measurements into one monotonic time domain.
Provide a global hardware timestamp unit with documented resolution and clock source.
Define master clock tolerance, sleep drift and resynchronization to a host epoch.
Prevent time-counter ambiguity or rollover over the longest approved logging session.
Support programmable triggers linking optical pulses, ADCs, electrochem, audio, IMU, GPIO and DMA.
Document each trigger-to-sample latency, jitter and clock crossing uncertainty.
Timestamp IMU samples at a defined sync point with FIFO delay correction.
Preserve documented physical IMU axes in package and product coordinates.
Verify reset-domain and clock-domain crossings and glitch-free clock changes.
Provide wake scheduling, on-body/contact monitoring and event-based host wake.
Supervise battery, low-rate temperature, watchdog, sensor duty-cycle and power-sequencing faults while host sleeps.
Minimize always-on energy at specified enabled sensor states.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET single-digit to tens of µW; mode TBD

Requirement: Keep high-energy sources and body drives disabled on reset and invalid power states.
Define for each power domain rails, reset, retention, isolation, wake source and entry/exit latency.
Implement POR, brownout, watchdog and host/PMIC fault reset behavior with deterministic startup.
Evaluate CIC/FIR/IIR and decimation accelerators only against measured processor energy and area.
Evaluate RMS, peak, correlation, FFT, lock-in and I/Q primitives for selected modes.
Validate fixed-point output against stated numeric error budgets for each implemented primitive.
Attach signal quality/state metadata such as saturation, gains, contact and calibration IDs to applicable streams.
Size local SRAM from concurrent FIFO bursts, DSP workspace and allowed host sleep time.
Report FIFO overflow or dropped frames with a monotonic timestamp and quality status.
Evaluate SRAM banks, retention, parity/ECC and BIST against fault and leakage budgets.
Evaluate nRF internal NVM, optional NOR, NAND and combinations by logging load and power.
Target_or_Limit: NOR candidate 256 Mb–1 Gb; NAND candidate 4–16 Gb

Requirement: Specify NAND throughput, endurance, retention and write energy under approved modes.
Provide error correction, bad-block handling, integrity and recovery if raw NAND is selected.
Protect sensitive stored measurements through secure authenticated/encrypted policy as required by product threat model.
Support a high-throughput nRF-to-ASIC data and control interface sized to worst approved sensor burst.
Support DMA-friendly framing, CRC, flow control and explicit overflow/error status.
Provide wake, interrupt, reset, boot and fault handshake semantics.
Control production debug access separately from authenticated operational paths.
Derive rail and battery design around measured usable energy for a very small wearable cell.
Provide programmable precharge, CC, CV, termination, recharge, storage and ship behavior for selected cell.
Enforce independent battery overvoltage, undervoltage, short, overcurrent and thermal protection.
Report voltage, current, temperature and coulomb count for runtime/SOC/SOH estimates.
Select buck/buck-boost/LDO/load switch counts using efficiency at actual mode currents.
Target_or_Limit: Candidate 2–3 buck; 4–6 LDO; other rails TBD

Requirement: Size optical/actuator boost separately or together based on noise and concurrent mode validity.
Allow external or co-packaged µH inductors where on-die passive performance is insufficient.
Quantify sensitive analog rail noise and switching spur rejection in all supported modes.
Record active, idle, retention, leakage, startup energy and peak current for every power domain.
Validate usable battery runtime with rail conversion losses, end-of-life and cold/peak sag.
Provide power state ordering, isolation and retention behavior across every domain transition.
Maintain transient PMIC headroom for future loads without materially reducing low-load efficiency.
Implement reverse-current blocking and battery-presence/fault behavior for the chosen charger topology.
Ensure shutdown and storage states meet usable battery shelf-life targets.
Keep electrode/drive, UV, high-current optical and audio/piezo outputs disabled on all resets until validated enable conditions.
Implement hardware exposure/current/temperature limits independent of host firmware for selected hazardous outputs.
Define body-connected ESD/EMC strategy jointly with leakage and electrode input error budgets.
Characterize latch-up and ESD behavior of separate quiet electrode and high-current pad classes.
Separate patient/user safety engineering from functional test coverage and obtain qualified review.
Define optical exposure using calibrated optical radiant output and accepted safety criteria rather than current-only proxy.
Provide low-noise reference and bias generation with test access for relevant analog paths.
Provide calibration/loopback access for ADC, DAC, TIA and electrode/optical path errors.
Store gain, offset, current, temperature and oscillator trims with identified device provenance.
Ensure trim and calibration provenance survives reset, provisioning and field logging.
Assign a unique device identity with controlled provisioning.
Coordinate secure boot, authenticated firmware and rollback policy across nRF and ASIC.
Restrict production debug and test-mode access through authenticated policy.
Prevent unauthenticated commands from enabling body drive or other safety-critical excitation.
Encrypt and authenticate sensitive logs/storage based on product privacy and threat requirements.
Define production test and calibration for every accepted analog block with threshold, time and yield impact.
Provide digital scan/ATPG and SRAM BIST consistent with security and power domains.
Provide analog stimulus, observability, loopback, references and converter self-test within pad constraints.
Control post-manufacturing test access so production features cannot bypass safety and security.
Evaluate fan-out/RDL/laminate/die-stacking partitions against actual die availability and assembly design rules.
Target_or_Limit: TARGET 6–8 mm by 6–8 mm; ≤1.2 mm aspirational

Requirement: Analyze ground return, substrate coupling, RF isolation and high-current loops adjacent to microvolt sensing.
Plan guard, well isolation, quiet references and analog placement using selected PDK isolation structures.
Retain external transducers and physically unsuitable inductors/optics rather than assuming CMOS integration.
Verify package parasitic, thermal, warpage, yield and test-access implications before package freeze.
Build first-principles, versioned energy, noise, data, timing, area/package and thermal budgets before architecture freeze.
State operating conditions, provenance, uncertainty and whether evidence is measured, simulated, calculated or assumed for each quantitative target.
Provide appropriate physical references, nuisance variables and statistics before upgrading a research biomarker claim.
Map every frozen ID to analysis, design, test evidence and review status before signoff.
Release mask data only after clean signoff or formally approved waivers, provenance, hashes and qualified review.
